description:
FILED s446i (Opus agent I), from the #509 probes.

REPRODUCERS (perl 5.40.3 on the left, PCL on the right):

    our %hh; $hh{a} = {b=>1};
    { local $hh{a}{b} = 6; print $hh{a}{b}; }
    print ",", $hh{a}{b}, "\n";
        perl  6,1
        PCL   CRASH: "Value of pcl::h in (sb-impl::gethash3 k h nil) is 6,
              not a hash-table" -- the emission is
              (p-local-hash-elem-init %hh "a" 6 â¦), i.e. it localized
              $hh{a} and ASSIGNED 6 TO IT, then $hh{a}{b} read through 6.

    our %h; our $p; $h{a}={b=>1};
    local ($p, $h{a}{b}) = (5,6);
        perl  5,6
        PCL   loud DROP: "Parser2 TODO: unsupported `local` target: $h{"a"}{"b"}"
              (s446i's rule-12 classifier; before s446i it was the same silent
              flattening as the single spelling)

CAUSE: Pl::Parser::_process_local_declaration's single-target branch matches
`@non_ws >= 2 && [0] Symbol && [1] Subscript` and takes $non_ws[1] as THE
subscript, ignoring any further ones; the `=` search then starts after it and
finds the initializer, so the chain's HEAD is localized and assigned the tail's
value.  s446i's _local_target_item (the LIST scan) refuses the shape instead of
flattening it, which is why the two spellings now fail differently.

SHAPE OF A FIX: a chained target is a PLACE like any other -- the container is
the chain minus its last subscript (`(p-gethash %hh "a")` dereferenced), the
key is the last subscript.  The element macros take a container FORM already
(the arrow branch passes `(unbox $ref_cl)`), so the work is building that form
from the chain, in ONE helper both the single branch and _local_target_item
call (they must not drift -- that IS this bug's family).

BAR: the two reproducers above plus `local $h{a}[0]`, `local $a[0]{k}`,
`local $r->{a}{b}`, the restore after the block, and the same six shapes inside
a `local` LIST; a Pl/t guard row in stmt-modifier-01.t or local-elem-02.t;
corpus-diff (no corpus site today -- grep found none in perl-tests, lib,
cpan-tests or perl's own t/).
subject: SILENT WRONG / CRASH: a CHAINED subscript as a `local` target localizes only the FIRST level -- `local $h{a}{b} = 6` installs 6 at $h{a} and then dies reading through it; in a `local` LIST the same shape now DROPS loudly (s446i)
